facts.statement: The genus of this dinosaur is Ankylosaurus.
facts.quote: genus: Ankylosaurus

facts.statement: The only known species is Ankylosaurus magniventris.
facts.quote: species: magniventris

facts.statement: The genus was named by Barnum Brown in 1908.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Brown, 1908

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous Period, approximately 70 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in geological formations dating to the very end of the Cretaceous Period, about 70-66 million years ago

facts.statement: Fossils of Ankylosaurus have been found in western North America.
facts.quote: in western North America

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus was a quadrupedal dinosaur with a broad and robust body.
facts.quote: It was quadrupedal, with a broad, robust body

facts.statement: The skull of Ankylosaurus was wide and low, featuring two backward-pointing horns on the back of the head and two additional horns below them pointing backward and downward.
facts.quote: It had a wide, low skull, with two horns pointing backward from the back of the head, and two horns below these that pointed backward and down

facts.statement: Unlike other ankylosaurs, the nostrils of Ankylosaurus faced sideways instead of forward.
facts.quote: Unlike other ankylosaurs, its nostrils faced sideways rather than towards the front

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus had a beak at the front of its jaws and rows of small, leaf-shaped teeth further back.
facts.quote: The front part of the jaws was covered in a beak, with rows of small, leaf-shaped teeth farther behind it

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus was covered in armor plates (osteoderms) with bony half-rings on the neck and a large club at the end of its tail.
facts.quote: It was covered in armor plates, or osteoderms, with bony half-rings covering the neck, and had a large club on the end of its tail

facts.statement: The broad muzzle of Ankylosaurus suggests it was a non-selective browser.
facts.quote: Its broad muzzle indicates it was a non-selective browser

facts.statement: Researchers believe the tail club was used for defense against predators or in fights with other Ankylosaurus.
facts.quote: The tail club is thought to have been used in defense against predators or in intraspecific combat

facts.statement: The type specimen of Ankylosaurus magniventris was discovered in 1906 by Barnum Brown in the Hell Creek Formation near Gilbert Creek, Montana.
facts.quote: In 1906, an American Museum of Natural History expedition led by American paleontologist Barnum Brown discovered the type specimen of Ankylosaurus magniventris (AMNH 5895) in the Hell Creek Formation, near Gilbert Creek, Montana

facts.statement: The type specimen consisted of the upper skull, two teeth, parts of the shoulder girdle and vertebrae, ribs, and over thirty osteoderms.
facts.quote: The specimen (found by collector Peter Kaisen) consisted of the upper part of a skull, two teeth, part of the shoulder girdle, cervical, dorsal, and caudal vertebrae, ribs, and more than thirty osteoderms (armor plates)

facts.statement: Barnum Brown scientifically described Ankylosaurus in 1908.
facts.quote: Brown scientifically described the animal in 1908

facts.statement: The genus name comes from Greek words meaning 'bent' or 'crooked' (referring to bone fusion) and 'lizard'.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from the Greek words αγκυλος ('bent' or 'crooked'), referring to the medical term ankylosis, the stiffness produced by the fusion of bones in the skull and body, and σαυρος ('lizard')

facts.statement: In 1910, Barnum Brown's expedition found an Ankylosaurus specimen in the Scollard Formation near the Red Deer River in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: In 1910, another AMNH expedition led by Brown discovered an Ankylosaurus specimen (AMNH 5214) in the Scollard Formation by the Red Deer River in Alberta, Canada

facts.statement: In 1947, Charles M. Sternberg and T. Potter Chamney collected a skull and mandible near the site of the 1910 discovery.
facts.quote: In 1947 the American fossil collectors Charles M. Sternberg and T. Potter Chamney collected a skull and mandible (specimen CMN 8880, formerly NMC 8880), 1 km north of where the 1910 specimen was found

facts.statement: A section of tail vertebrae was discovered in the 1960s in the Powder River drainage of Montana.
facts.quote: A section of caudal vertebrae (specimen CCM V03) was discovered in the 1960s in the Powder River drainage, Montana, part of the Hell Creek Formation

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus is possibly the largest known ankylosaurid, estimated at 6 to 8 meters long and weighing 4.8 to 8 metric tons.
facts.quote: Possibly the largest known ankylosaurid, Ankylosaurus is estimated to have been between 6 and 8 m long and to have weighed between 4.8 and 8 MT

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus fossils have been found in the Hell Creek, Lance, Scollard, Frenchman, and Ferris formations.
facts.quote: Specimens of Ankylosaurus have been found in the Hell Creek, Lance, Scollard, Frenchman, and Ferris formations

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that Ankylosaurus may have inhabited upland areas.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus may have inhabited upland areas

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus is considered the largest known ankylosaurine dinosaur and possibly the largest ankylosaurid.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus was the largest-known ankylosaurine dinosaur and possibly the largest ankylosaurid.

facts.statement: In 2014, Benson and colleagues estimated the weight of the smallest known Ankylosaurus specimen (AMNH 5214) at 4.78 metric tons.
facts.quote: The English paleontologist Roger B. J. Benson and colleagues estimated the weight for AMNH 5214 at 4.78 MT in 2014.

facts.statement: Arbour and Mallon tentatively estimated the weight of the largest Ankylosaurus specimen (CMN 8880) at 7.95 metric tons.
facts.quote: Arbour and Mallon estimated a weight of 4.78 MT for AMNH 5214, and tentatively estimated the weight of CMN 8880 at 7.95 MT.

facts.statement: The Ankylosaurus skull was low, triangular, and wider than it was long, with a broad and low rear.
facts.quote: The skull was low and triangular in shape, and wider than it was long; the back of the skull was broad and low.

facts.statement: Crests above the eye sockets merged into pyramidal-shaped upper squamosal horns that pointed backward and to the sides from the rear of the skull.
facts.quote: Crests above the orbits merged into the upper squamosal horns (their shape has been described as "pyramidal"), which pointed backwards to the sides from the back of the skull.

facts.statement: Large, strap-like osteoderms on the snout completely covered the nostril openings, giving them a bulbous appearance.
facts.quote: Large loreal caputegulae—strap-like, side osteoderms of the snout—completely roofed the enlarged opening of the nostrils, giving a bulbous appearance.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus possessed small, leaf-shaped teeth that were compressed sideways.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus had small, phylliform (leaf-shaped) teeth, which were compressed sideways.

facts.statement: The denticles on Ankylosaurus teeth were large, numbering six to eight on the front part and five to seven on the rear part.
facts.quote: The denticles were large, their number ranging from six to eight on the front part of the tooth, and five to seven behind.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus was a quadruped with hind limbs longer than its forelimbs.
facts.quote: It was quadrupedal, and its hind limbs were longer than its forelimbs.

facts.statement: In the holotype specimen, the shoulder blade measured 61.5 centimeters long and was fused with the coracoid bone.
facts.quote: In the holotype specimen, the scapula (shoulder blade) measures 61.5 cm long and was fused with the coracoid (a rectangular bone connected to the lower end of the scapula).

facts.statement: The thigh bone of the smallest Ankylosaurus specimen (AMNH 5214) was 67 centimeters long and very robust.
facts.quote: The femur (thigh bone), also from AMNH 5214, was 67 cm long and very robust.

facts.statement: The hind feet of Ankylosaurus likely had three toes, consistent with advanced ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: The hindfeet probably had three toes, as is the case in advanced ankylosaurids.

facts.statement: The presence of fleshy cheeks in ornithischians is controversial, though some related nodosaurs had armor plates covering the cheek region.
facts.quote: the presence of cheeks in ornithischians is controversial, but some nodosaurs had armor plates that covered the cheek region, which may have been embedded in the flesh.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus had armor made of bone knobs and plates called osteoderms embedded in its skin.
facts.quote: A prominent feature of Ankylosaurus was its armor, consisting of knobs and plates of bone known as osteoderms, or scutes, embedded in the skin.

facts.statement: The osteoderms of Ankylosaurus were generally thin-walled and hollowed on the underside.
facts.quote: The osteoderms of Ankylosaurus were generally thin walled and hollowed on the underside.

facts.statement: The tail club of the largest Ankylosaurus specimen may have been 57 cm wide.
facts.quote: The club of the largest specimen may have been 57 cm wide.

facts.statement: The range of variation in Ankylosaurus tail clubs is unknown because only the club from specimen AMNH 5214 is known.
facts.quote: As only the tail club of specimen AMNH 5214 is known, the range of variation between individuals is unknown.

facts.statement: Osborn coined the name Ankylosauria in 1923 to place ankylosaurids in their own suborder.
facts.quote: In 1923 Osborn coined the name Ankylosauria, thereby placing the ankylosaurids in their own suborder.

facts.statement: Ankylosauria and Stegosauria are grouped together within the clade Thyreophora.
facts.quote: Ankylosauria and Stegosauria are now grouped together within the clade Thyreophora.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus is considered part of the subfamily Ankylosaurinae within the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus is considered part of the subfamily Ankylosaurinae (members of which are called ankylosaurines) within Ankylosauridae.

facts.statement: Carpenter suggested that Ankylosaurus neck armor formed an inverted V-shape with a midline gap filled by small ossicles to allow movement.
facts.quote: Carpenter suggested that when seen from above, the plates would have been paired, creating an inverted V-shape across the neck, with the midline gap probably being filled with small ossicles (round bony scutes) to allow for movement.

facts.statement: Arbour and Currie disagreed with Carpenter's 2015 interpretation of Ankylosaurus neck armor, noting that the holotype fragments did not fit as Carpenter proposed.
facts.quote: Arbour and the Canadian paleontologist Philip J. Currie disagreed with Carpenter's interpretation in 2015 and pointed out that the cervical half-ring fragments of the holotype specimen did not fit together in the way proposed by Carpenter (though this could be due to breakage).

facts.statement: Arbour and Currie suggested that Ankylosaurus neck armor consisted of two semi-circular plates around the upper neck, similar to Anodontosaurus and Euoplocephalus.
facts.quote: They instead suggested that the fragments represented the remains of two cervical half-rings, which formed two semi-circular plates of armor around the upper part of the neck, as in the closely related Anodontosaurus and Euoplocephalus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Ankylosaurus had a shorter tail relative to its body or the same proportions but a smaller club compared to other ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: The larger width may indicate that the tail of Ankylosaurus was shorter in relation to its body length than those of other ankylosaurids, or that it had the same proportions but with a smaller club.

facts.statement: Arbour and Currie suggested that earlier North American ankylosaurids went extinct by the late Albian or Cenomanian ages.
facts.quote: Arbour and Currie suggested that earlier North American ankylosaurids had gone extinct by the late Albian or Cenomanian ages of the Middle Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Arbour and Currie suggested that ankylosaurids recolonized North America from Asia during the Campanian or Turonian ages, leading to the diversification of genera like Ankylosaurus.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurids thereafter recolonized North America from Asia during the Campanian or Turonian ages of the Late Cretaceous, and there diversified again, leading to genera such as Ankylosaurus, Anodontosaurus, and Euoplocephalus.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus was a herbivore.
facts.quote: Like other ornithischians, Ankylosaurus was herbivorous.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurus likely fed on abundant ferns and low-growing shrubs.
facts.quote: Ankylosaurus probably fed on abundant ferns and low-growing shrubs.

facts.statement: If Ankylosaurus was endothermic, it would have consumed approximately 60 kg of ferns per day.
facts.quote: Assuming it was endothermic, Ankylosaurus would have eaten 60 kg of ferns per day, similar to the amount of dry vegetation a large elephant would consume.

facts.statement: In 1982, Carpenter described two baby Ankylosaurus teeth from the Lance and Hell Creek Formations measuring 3.2 to 3.3 mm in length.
facts.quote: In 1982 Carpenter ascribed to baby Ankylosaurus two very small teeth that originate from the Lance and Hell Creek Formations and measure 3.2 to 3.3 mm in length, respectively.

facts.statement: Because adult Ankylosaurus did little chewing, it likely spent less time foraging than an elephant.
facts.quote: Since adult Ankylosaurus did little chewing of its food, it would have spent less time in the day foraging than an elephant.

facts.statement: In 1969, Georg Haas concluded that ankylosaur skull musculature was relatively weak despite the large skull size.
facts.quote: In 1969, paleontologist Georg Haas concluded that despite the large size of ankylosaur skulls, the associated musculature was relatively weak.

facts.statement: A 2016 study suggests that the ability for backwards jaw movement evolved independently in ankylosaur lineages including Ankylosaurus.
facts.quote: A 2016 study of the dental occlusion (contact between the teeth) of ankylosaur specimens found that the ability for backwards (palinal) jaw movement evolved independently in different ankylosaur lineages, including Late Cretaceous North American ankylosaurids like Ankylosaurus and Euoplocephalus.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Ankylosaurus may have been omnivorous based on its low tooth formation rate and other factors.
facts.quote: These factors, as well as the low rate of tooth formation in ankylosaurs compared to other ornithischians, indicate that Ankylosaurus may have been omnivorous (eating both plant and animal matter).

facts.statement: A 2023 study found that Ankylosaurus had jaws with low mechanical advantage compared to its earlier relatives.
facts.quote: A 2023 study by paleontologist Antonio Ballell and colleagues found that North American ankylosaurids from the latest Cretaceous (including Ankylosaurus) had jaws with low mechanical advantage, whereas those of earlier relatives were high to moderate.

facts.statement: In 1977, Teresa Maryańska proposed that ankylosaur nasal cavities may have lightened the skull, housed a gland, or aided vocal resonance.
facts.quote: In 1977, paleontologist Teresa Maryańska proposed that the complex sinuses and nasal cavities of ankylosaurs may have lightened the weight of the skull, housed a nasal gland, or acted as a chamber for vocal resonance.

facts.statement: Carpenter rejected the idea that ankylosaur sinuses were used for weight reduction or vocal resonance.
facts.quote: Carpenter rejected these hypotheses, arguing that tetrapod animals make sounds through the larynx, not the nostrils, and that reduction in weight was minimal, as the spaces only accounted for a small percent of the skull volume.

facts.statement: Inner ear reconstructions suggest Ankylosaurus was adapted to hear low frequencies.
facts.quote: Reconstructions of the inner ear suggest adaptation to hearing at low frequencies, such as the low-toned resonant sounds possibly produced by the nasal passages.

facts.statement: Ankylosaurids had an enlarged olfactory region indicating a well-developed sense of smell.
facts.quote: The enlarged olfactory region of ankylosaurids indicates a well-developed sense of smell.

facts.statement: Carpenter suggested Ankylosaurus nasal airflow was likely unidirectional, though bidirectional flow in the posterior chamber is possible.
facts.quote: According to Carpenter, the shape of the nasal chambers of Ankylosaurus indicate that airflow was unidirectional (looping through the lungs during inhalation and exhalation), although it may also have been bidirectional in the posterior nasal chamber, with air directed past the olfactory lobes.

facts.statement: The position of Ankylosaurus orbits suggests it had some stereoscopic vision.
facts.quote: The position of the orbits of Ankylosaurus suggest some stereoscopic vision.
